{{See also|Upcoming features|Matcha Flavoured 1.12.2#Post-release fixes}}
This page lists '''known bugs''' in [[Matcha Flavoured]]: places where the pack's code does something it evidently isn't meant to, such as text that shows a raw translation key, tooltips that disagree with an item's real values, and mechanics that don't match the release notes. Each entry was found by reading the pack's source for the current release, {{Version|1.12.6-alpha}}. The README asks players to report bugs through the feedback form it links.<ref>{{Source|README.md}}</ref> Bugs fixed in earlier versions are listed in each article's History section and on the [[Version history|version pages]].

== Untranslated text ==
When a text component asks for a translation key that the resource pack's language file doesn't define, the game shows the key itself. The following keys are used by the datapack but missing from <code>en_us.json</code>:<ref>{{Source|MF_resourcepack/assets/minecraft/lang/en_us.json}}</ref>
{| class="wikitable"
! Where it shows !! Missing key !! Notes
|-
| "Repaired with" line of the [[Elytra#Shakudo Elytra|shakudo elytra]] || <code>item.minecraft.copper_block</code> || The vanilla key is <code>block.minecraft.copper_block</code>, which the hepatizon elytra uses correctly.<ref>{{Source|MF_datapack/data/matcha/recipe/smithing/shakudo_elytra.json}}</ref>
|-
| Nowhere in practice || <code>item.kleispack.fish.axolotl</code> || Used by the loot table <code>gameplay/fishing/fish/axolotl</code>, which no other table calls. The junk table's axolotl uses <code>item.kleispack.axolotl</code>, which exists.<ref>{{Source|MF_datapack/data/minecraft/loot_table/gameplay/fishing/fish/axolotl.json}}</ref><ref>{{Source|MF_datapack/data/minecraft/loot_table/gameplay/fishing/junk.json}}</ref>
|}

Each item's article cites the file. Other tooltip problems:
* The [[Elytra#Shakudo Elytra|shakudo elytra]]'s tooltip promises an "Elytra Bonus" of 10 seconds off the shakudo regeneration timer, but the item carries the ordinary shakudo armor intrinsic, so it only counts as one more shakudo piece. A separate <code>matcha:shakudo_elytra</code> intrinsic exists but isn't on the item.<ref>{{Source|MF_datapack/data/matcha/recipe/smithing/shakudo_elytra.json}}</ref> The {{Version|1.12.2}} notes list "Shakudo Elytra Bonus was not working" as fixed.<ref>{{Cite changelog|1.12.2|quote=Shakudo Elytra Bonus was not working (not sure how this was deleted)}}</ref>
* The [[Adamant Pickaxe|adamant pickaxe]] lists [[divinity]] under "Set Bonus:", but tools don't count toward the set bonus. See [[Divinity]].

== Mechanics ==
* '''No Fortune on the tips of cave vines.''' The {{Version|1.12.2}} notes say Fortune now works on tomatoes, glow berry vines and chorus plants.<ref>{{Cite changelog|1.12.2|quote=Fortune now works on: Tomatoes, Glow berry vines, Chorus Plant}}</ref> It does on cave vine bodies, but not on the berry-bearing tip block (<code>cave_vines</code>), whose table lost its Fortune and [[Electrum equipment|electrum]] bonuses in 1.12.3.<ref>{{Source|MF_datapack/data/minecraft/loot_table/blocks/cave_vines.json}}</ref><ref>{{Source|MF_datapack/data/minecraft/loot_table/blocks/cave_vines_plant.json}}</ref>
* '''No Fortune on tomatoes and chorus plants.''' The tomato (beetroot) and chorus plant tables apply the Fortune and electrum bonuses and then set a fixed count (1–3 tomatoes, 0–1 chorus fruit), which replaces them, as in 1.12.2. 1.12.3 had fixed the order, but the 26.3 tables in 1.12.6-alpha went back to it. See [[Tomatoes]] and [[Chorus Fruit]].<ref>{{Source|MF_datapack/data/minecraft/loot_table/blocks/beetroots.json}}</ref><ref>{{Source|MF_datapack/data/minecraft/loot_table/blocks/chorus_plant.json}}</ref>
* '''No Fortune on native gold's raw gold.''' The raw gold entry of the stone [[Native Gold|native gold]] table is still in the 26.2 format (<code>functions</code> instead of <code>modifier</code>). ''Minecraft'' 26.3 doesn't read that key, so the raw gold gets neither the Fortune nor the electrum bonus and is always 1. Native deepslate gold is unaffected.<ref>{{Source|MF_datapack/data/minecraft/loot_table/blocks/gold_ore.json}}</ref>
* '''Glow berries from bare vines.''' The cave vine tables (<code>cave_vines</code> and <code>cave_vines_plant</code>) have no check for whether the vine carries berries, unlike vanilla, so every broken cave vine block drops glow berries.<ref>{{Source|MF_datapack/data/minecraft/loot_table/blocks/cave_vines.json}}</ref>
* '''Silent fished crystal hearts.''' The treasure sound checks for the item model <code>matcha:crystal_heart</code>, but fished [[Crystal Heart|crystal hearts]] use <code>matcha:heart_container</code>, so catching one plays no sound. See [[Fishing sounds#Bugs]].<ref>{{Source|MF_datapack/data/matcha/advancement/fishing_sounds/treasure.json}}</ref>
* '''Incomplete Angler's Almanac.''' The junk category of the [[Angler's Almanac]] has entries for a bowl and a tripwire hook, but no fishing table can give either, so the tab can't be completed.<ref>{{Source|MF_datapack/data/matcha/advancement/anglers_almanac/junk/bowl.json}}</ref><ref>{{Source|MF_datapack/data/minecraft/loot_table/gameplay/fishing/junk.json}}</ref>
* '''Plain bones become fish bones.''' The item updater's fish bones check accepts any bone without the pack's version tag, so a plain bone held in either hand, such as one dropped by a skeleton, is renamed to [[Fish Bones|fish bones]] the next time the inventory changes. It still works as a bone.<ref>{{Source|MF_datapack/data/matcha_item/advancement/trigger/fish_bones.json}}</ref><ref>{{Source|MF_datapack/data/matcha_item/predicate/mainhand/fish_bones.json}}</ref><ref>{{Source|MF_datapack/data/matcha_item/item_modifier/modify/fish_bones.json}}</ref>
* '''Milking a mooshroom clears every player's mushroom stew.''' Using a bowl on a mooshroom gives [[Clear Mushroom Soup|clear mushroom soup]], then runs <code>clear @a minecraft:mushroom_stew[minecraft:max_stack_size=1]</code> for all players. It runs on any use of a bowl on a mooshroom.<ref>{{Source|MF_datapack/data/matcha/function/mechanics/mooshroom_milking/replace_chocolate_with_soup.mcfunction}}</ref>
* '''Vanilla foods can't be eaten on a full food bar.''' The pack's own foods have no food component, so they can always be eaten.<ref>{{Source|MF_datapack/data/matcha/loot_table/food/minecraft/bread.json}}</ref> Items the pack leaves as they are in vanilla, such as raw meats, and vanilla or modded foods from elsewhere (the creative menu, other mods) keep theirs, so as in vanilla they can only be eaten while the food bar isn't full. Until 1.12.5 a hidden Hunger effect kept the bar from filling; since {{Version|1.12.6-alpha}}, which gives the Hunger effect a use, the pack only tops the bar up with Saturation when it falls to 8 or lower, so the bar can fill up and these foods then can't be eaten.<ref>{{Source|MF_datapack/data/matcha/function/mechanics/manage_hunger.mcfunction}}</ref> The 1.12.6-alpha notes list this as expected: old foods "may sometimes be inedible", vanilla foods from the creative menu are inedible "unless they update automatically", raw meats are inedible, and modded foods sometimes are. They ask players to report newly crafted or cooked foods that can't be eaten.<ref>{{Cite changelog|1.12.6-alpha|quote=If you use vanilla foods (Ie. from the creative menu) they will be inedible (unless they update automatically)}}</ref>
* '''Iron chain recipe never unlocks.''' Picking up iron ingots is meant to unlock the recipe that turns 3 iron ingots into 18 [[chain]]s, but the unlock names <code>iron_chain_from_iron</code>, while the recipe is <code>iron_chain_from_ingot</code>. The recipe works when placed by hand but never appears in the recipe book.<ref>{{Source|MF_datapack/data/matcha/advancement/recipe_unlocks/iron_ingot.json}}</ref><ref>{{Source|MF_datapack/data/matcha/recipe/crafting/iron_chain_from_ingot.json}}</ref>
* '''Toadstool recipes never unlock.''' Obtaining a [[Braised Toadstool|braised toadstool]] is meant to unlock the [[Pickled Toadstools|pickled toadstools]] and [[Toadstool Stroganoff|toadstool stroganoff]] recipes, but the check looks for the item model <code>braised_red_mushroom</code> (read as <code>minecraft:braised_red_mushroom</code>), while the braised toadstool's model is <code>matcha:braised_red_mushroom</code>. Nothing else unlocks the two recipes, so they never appear in the recipe book, though they can still be crafted.<ref>{{Source|MF_datapack/data/matcha/advancement/recipe_unlocks/braised_red_mushroom.json}}</ref><ref>{{Source|MF_datapack/data/matcha/recipe/food/oven/braised_red_mushroom.json}}</ref>
* '''Early pickaxes mine ancient debris.''' The pack's pickaxes list <code>#minecraft:mineable/pickaxe</code> as correct for drops without a tier check, and the blocks each tier ''can't'' mine are listed by hand. Ancient debris isn't on any of those lists, so even a wooden pickaxe gets it. See [[Tools#Mining levels]].<ref>{{Source|MF_datapack/data/matcha/tags/block/non_mineable/wood.json}}</ref>
* '''Mobs keep their spawn equipment drops.''' The pack means to set the drop chances of the armor and weapons that hostile mobs spawn with to 0, but the command targets <code>@n</code> (the nearest matching mob) from a function that runs as the new mob without running at its position, so it changes the matching mob nearest the world spawn point instead. Most mobs keep their vanilla chance to drop that gear. See [[Spawning]].<ref>{{Source|MF_datapack/data/matcha/function/mechanics/spawn_mechanic/clear_drop_chances.mcfunction}}</ref><ref>{{Source|MF_datapack/data/matcha/function/mechanics/spawn_mechanic/check_mob_spawn.mcfunction}}</ref>
* '''Favorite food trades aren't limited to one use.''' 41 of the 42 [[favorite food]] functions write the offer's use limit as <code>max_uses</code>, but the game reads villager offers' limit from <code>maxUses</code>, so the limit of 1 is ignored and the game's default applies. Only the apple empanada's function uses the right key.<ref>{{Source|MF_datapack/data/matcha/function/favorite_food/food_trades/food_2.mcfunction}}</ref><ref>{{Source|MF_datapack/data/matcha/function/favorite_food/food_trades/food_0.mcfunction}}</ref> The repository's 26.3 branch fixed this after the release; its changelog calls it a bug "that resulted in high restock rates".<ref>{{Source|MF_datapack/data/matcha/function/favorite_food/food_trades/food_2.mcfunction|at=40041671de14b05fa8261cc33845c7f5b1afdc65}}</ref><ref>{{Cite changelog|quote=Villager trade favourite foods had a bug that resulted in high restock rates}}</ref>
* '''Glass bottles lost when crafting stroganoff.''' The advancement that gives back a milk bottle's glass bottle after crafting does not list [[Stroganoff|stroganoff]], toadstool stroganoff or [[Crimson Stroganoff|crimson stroganoff]], so crafting any of these uses up the bottle. [[Warped Stroganoff|Warped stroganoff]] is listed and gives its bottle back.<ref>{{Source|MF_datapack/data/matcha/advancement/mechanics/glass_bottle_from_crafting.json}}</ref>
* '''The item updater doesn't restore enchantments.''' The [[Updating items|item updater]] gathers each item's standard enchantment levels and then calls <code>matcha_item:enchants/&lt;slot&gt;</code> to apply them. Until 1.12.6-alpha those functions didn't exist under that name, so the call was skipped. Since 1.12.6-alpha they exist, but they write the item modifier inline with the key <code>function</code>, the ''Minecraft'' 26.2 form; in 26.3 the key is <code>type</code> (the pack's own item modifier files changed to it in the same release), so the command fails and updated items still keep the enchantments they had. The off-hand function would also change the main-hand item.<ref>{{Source|MF_datapack/data/matcha_item/function/mainhand/adamant_axe.mcfunction}}</ref><ref>{{Source|MF_datapack/data/matcha_item/function/enchants/mainhand.mcfunction}}</ref><ref>{{Source|MF_datapack/data/matcha_item/function/enchants/offhand.mcfunction}}</ref><ref>{{Source|MF_datapack/data/matcha/item_modifier/fox_pelt.json}}</ref>

== Other ==
* '''Loot-table steel shears are a shovel.''' The [[Steel Shears|steel shears]] are made by smithing ordinary shears, and the updater for old items also turns them into shears,<ref>{{Source|MF_datapack/data/matcha/recipe/smithing/steel_shears.json}}</ref><ref>{{Source|MF_datapack/data/matcha/function/update_old_items/update_held_item.mcfunction}}</ref> but the loot table <code>matcha:equipment/steel/shears</code> builds them on a stone shovel, which can't shear. No other table or function rolls that table, so it only matters when it is given with <code>/loot</code>.<ref>{{Source|MF_datapack/data/matcha/loot_table/equipment/steel/shears.json}}</ref>
* '''Two different Labyrinthine discs.''' The crafted Labyrinthine [[Music Disc|music disc]] is built on disc "cat", but the one found in stronghold corridors is built on disc "11".<ref>{{Source|MF_datapack/data/matcha/recipe/crafting/music_disc_labyrinthine.json}}</ref><ref>{{Source|MF_datapack/data/matcha/loot_table/music_disc/labyrinthine.json}}</ref><ref>{{Source|MF_datapack/data/minecraft/loot_table/chests/stronghold_corridor.json}}</ref> Both play the same song and look the same, but the game treats them as different items: they don't stack together, and recipes or trades that check the disc type see a different disc.
* '''Darker trim colors never show.''' The resource pack has darker trim palettes for armor trimmed with its own alloy (<code>electrum_darker</code>, <code>shakudo_darker</code>, <code>hepatizon_darker</code>), and the inventory icons of such armor ask for them, but its atlases map those names to the normal palettes, so such trims look the same as on other armor. Since 1.12.6-alpha the trim materials no longer ask for a darker palette on worn armor at all. See [[Trims]].<ref>{{Source|MF_resourcepack/assets/minecraft/atlases/armor_trims.json}}</ref><ref>{{Source|MF_resourcepack/assets/matcha/models/item/shakudo_helmet_shakudo_trim.json}}</ref>

== Acknowledged by the developer ==
The README lists one major known bug: on Purpur servers, and possibly others, <code>keep_inventory</code> is handled per dimension, so it has to be set by command in each dimension or items are lost on death.<ref>{{Source|README.md}}</ref> See [[Multiplayer]].

The in-development changelog lists these as low-priority bugs that aren't fixed yet:<ref>{{Cite changelog|quote=Add predicate for surface spawn that excludes structures}}</ref>
* The post-dragon [[Surface|safe-surface]] check doesn't exclude structures in general (only trial chambers and the [[Abbey]] are exempt).
* [[Trailblaze]] boots gave their speed boost on mud brick slabs when jumping, but not when simply running on them. 1.12.6-alpha reworked how the boost is applied; see [[Trailblaze#Speed]].
* The toolsmith's hero-of-the-village gift is still stone tools, which the pack otherwise removes.
